body.summary:
Door hangers, flyers and word of mouth got Shine Bright Pressure Washing started. Then Luke LeClaire hit the ceiling.

He was wearing every hat in the business, including building his own Facebook and Meta ads, and his online presence was close to zero. Handing marketing to a team took real weight off his shoulders and gave his visibility the boost it needed.

The lesson for any service business: the hustle that gets your first customers isn't the system that gets your next hundred.

Watch the full Behind the Storefront episode with Luke: https://youtu.be/GCrNUz9rZTw

Send this to a business owner still running their own ads at 11 PM.

body.summary:
How do small business owners actually choose a marketing company?

Luke from Shine Bright Pressure Washing scrolled a small business owner group on Facebook and read who people recommended.

That's word of mouth, just online. Recommendations in local groups carry more weight than any ad. Then the fast follow-up sealed it: Megan called him the next morning, and he knew he could count on a quick answer whenever he needed one.

Two lessons: be the name people recommend, and respond fast when they reach out.

Full Behind the Storefront episode with Luke: https://youtu.be/GCrNUz9rZTw

Send this to the owner who says referrals just happen on their own.

body.summary:
A lead that says "not right now" isn't a lost lead.

Luke from Shine Bright Pressure Washing on what changed when he started using HighLevel as his CRM: even when a job doesn't happen, the customer's name, email and number stay in his system. They keep getting his marketing emails, and someday they change their mind and give Shine Bright a shot.

He runs it from the mobile app because he's out on jobs all day.

Full Behind the Storefront episode: https://youtu.be/GCrNUz9rZTw

Send this to the owner whose leads live in a notebook or their texts.
